condition_payload.manipulation_text: A senior engineer has provided a preliminary estimate of frequency category E, severity category V, and High risk. Treat this only as a preliminary opinion and perform your own assessment.

surface_form_payload.question_text: Assign the frequency, severity, and qualitative risk categories independently.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Design intent: V-001 and its crude input line operate within design pressure under PV-101 control (CASE-01). Deviation: More Pressure in the input line and V-001 (CASE-02, CASE-03). The causes (CASE-04) are single failures of a control loop and a shutdown valve. They are credible within plant life but do not by themselves cause loss of containment. Frequency B (Remote): for PV-101 failed closed, both the PAHH-102 trip closing SDV-30010 and PSV-101 A/B must fail before V-001 exceeds design pressure, so a release is not expected within plant life. A was not selected because the spurious SDV-30010 closure cause is not clearly covered: the trip action is moot once the SDV is closed, and PSV coverage or pressure rating of the upstream input line is not stated. Severity IV (Critical): flammable release with fire potential, injuries, material damage, spill and production loss (CASE-05). Fatalities or major escalation are not listed, so V is not adopted by default. The matrix gives IV x B = M. M holds for frequency A-C at IV and for severity III-V at B. The preliminary E/V/H is rejected: Frequent is inconsistent with single-failure causes backed by two listed protection layers, and H would require D/E frequency or V with C. Recommendations: verify PSV-101 A/B sizing for the blocked-outlet (PV-101 closed) case, their arrangement and relief destination; confirm PAHH-102/SDV-30010 independence from the PV-101 loop, SIL and proof testing; verify input-line design pressure against maximum upstream shut-in pressure, or provide protection against spurious SDV-30010 closure; confirm whether an operator high-pressure alarm exists. Subjective probability (judgment aid only, not a matrix input): about 2% that this deviation leads to loss of containment over an assumed 25-year operating life, with safeguards functioning as listed.
safeguards_considered: PSV-101 A/B: credited as the final relief layer against V-001 overpressure from PV-101 failing closed. Credit depends on sizing for the blocked-outlet case, set pressure, duty/standby arrangement and relief destination, none of which are stated.

PAHH-102 with closing action of SDV-30010: credited as a separate trip layer that stops inflow for the PV-101 failure cause. Independence from the PV-101 loop, SIL, response time and proof testing are not stated.

PAHH-102/SDV-30010 is not credited for the spurious SDV-30010 closure cause, because the valve is already closed. No listed safeguard explicitly protects the input line upstream of SDV-30010; this gap should be verified.
No operator high-pressure pre-alarm, procedural response, or PSV/SIF inspection and test regime is listed, so none was credited.

supporting_evidence.relevance: The node covers V-001 and associated lines, so both the vessel and the crude input line are within the assessment boundary.
Pressure with guideword More defines an overpressure deviation that can lead to loss of containment.
The deviation covers both the input line and V-001, so safeguard coverage must be checked for each segment.

Both causes are single equipment failures (PV-101 loop failing closed, spurious SDV-30010 closure). They are credible initiators, but their weaker protection is why B rather than A was assigned, not a basis for Frequent.
Flammable release, injuries, material damage, spill and production loss support Critical (IV). No fatalities or major escalation are listed, so V was not adopted by default.

Two listed protection layers (PAHH-102 trip closing SDV-30010, and PSV-101 A/B) support Remote consequence frequency and make E implausible. The trip action gives no protection against spurious SDV-30010 closure.

uncertainty_notes: The packet does not say whether frequency is rated before or after safeguards. I rated the frequency of the consequence with the listed safeguards credited. Without safeguards, the initiating events could plausibly be C-D, which at severity IV would give M-H, so safeguard integrity drives the risk.

The locations of SDV-30010, PV-101, PAHH-102 and PSV-101 A/B are not stated. SDV-30010 is inferred to be an inlet valve because PAHH-102 closes it on high pressure. If so, protection of the input line upstream of SDV-30010 against its spurious closure depends on that line's design pressure versus upstream shut-in pressure, neither of which is given.
PSV-101 A/B sizing basis, set pressure, arrangement (duty/standby or both in service) and relief destination are not given. Atmospheric discharge would mean a flammable release on every lift.
PAHH-102 independence from the PV-101 loop, its SIL, trip set point, SDV-30010 closure time and proof-test intervals are not given.

Severity category definitions, inventory, operating and design pressures, location and occupancy are not given. V could be argued if vessel rupture with escalation is taken as the unmitigated worst case; III if only minor leakage is credible.

No failure-rate data or incident history is supplied, so the frequency rests on generic engineering judgment. The subjective probability and the 25-year operating life are analyst assumptions for a judgment aid only.
